questions.q: Which of the following is an example of alternative data as covered in this lesson?
options: A company's quarterly 10-K filing
Satellite imagery used to count cars in retail parking lots
A stock's closing price on the exchange
A standard moving-average technical indicator
questions.explain: Satellite imagery (e.g., counting cars in parking lots to estimate foot traffic) is a classic example of alternative data -- a non-traditional source outside prices, filings, and news.

questions.q: Why does an alternative data source's information edge tend to erode over time?
options: Satellites eventually run out of fuel
As more funds discover and license the same dataset, more capital trades on the same signal, and the resulting price impact erodes the edge
Alternative data is always illegal after one year
Alt data vendors are required to stop selling data after it becomes profitable
questions.explain: The edge alt data provides fades the same way any discovered market inefficiency gets arbitraged away -- as more participants trade on the same information, its predictive value erodes.

questions.q: Why does short data history limit confidence in alt-data-driven signals specifically?
options: Short history makes computation faster but less accurate
Chapter 4's validation toolkit (purged walk-forward CV, deflated Sharpe) assumes enough independent time periods to validate across, which a 2-3 year dataset often can't provide
Short history always means the data is illegal to use
Short history prevents any model from being fit at all
questions.explain: Robust multi-regime validation, as taught in Chapter 4, requires enough independent historical periods. Many alternative datasets only have a couple of years of clean history, which limits how much validation confidence is possible.

questions.q: What is survivorship bias in the context of an alternative data vendor's panel?
options: A vendor backfilling coverage for currently-existing companies while silently omitting companies that went bankrupt or were delisted, flattering historical backtests
A vendor only covering companies founded within the last year
A bias that only affects satellite imagery data
A method used to improve data quality
questions.explain: Survivorship bias occurs when a dataset's historical coverage quietly excludes failed or delisted companies, making a backtest look better than live trading would actually have performed.

questions.q: What is material non-public information (MNPI), and why does it matter for alternative data sourcing?
options: Information that is publicly available on a company's website, which is always safe to trade on
Information that would move a security's price if disclosed and isn't available to the public; trading on it is illegal regardless of how it was obtained
A category of data that only applies to bonds, not equities
A term describing data that is too old to be useful
questions.explain: MNPI is price-moving information not available to the public. Trading on it is illegal no matter the source, so any new alternative data stream needs a compliance review to confirm it doesn't cross this line.
